doc.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024

chapter: The trombone and the business today
title: Creating your own lane in a tough business
summary: Davis says the music business is unhealthy but success is possible by creating your own lane instead of waiting for the phone.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: I’m happy to hear you say that because some people take the other attitude that the music business is in the pits and so forth, and I’m glad to hear you optimistic about it.

It is — those people are right. It’s not a tremendously healthy business but those people that want to get into it and are committed to doing the work, you can do it. You know, you can. And is it the same, you know, my generation you had to be a good player but it was really about answering the phone. You know it was about, hey, once I develop a good reputation there was enough work and loyalty and everything else that went along with it, all I had to do was answer the phone, say yes, and go to the jobs. It wasn’t quite that simple but once I got established that’s kind of what it was. Now you have to create your own lane. And that’s a much wider challenge. But when you do, and if you do, you control that lane which is great. I’d much rather be in control of my own destiny, especially if I’m able to survive as a professional musician, than rely on a contractor X, Y or Z who you hope you stay in their good graces and they don’t find somebody else,

‘cause they will, that they’d rather use and somebody else over here. So that’s the advantage right now is if you can create your own lane and have success with it I think the longevity is going to be there.
